title: Secondary Air Injection System Malfunction (Extended)
shortDescription: PCM does not see the expected oxygen response when SAI is commanded ON.
fullDescription: PCM does not see the expected oxygen response when SAI is commanded ON. The secondary air injection system pumps fresh air into the exhaust during cold start to help the catalytic converter light off. Carbon build-up in the check valves and corrosion in the pump are the most common root causes — particularly in cold-climate vehicles.
safetyImpact: Vehicle remains drivable. Long-term, an SAI fault prevents catalyst warm-up and increases cold-start emissions.

causes.cause: Failed SAI pump (water ingress / brush wear)
Failed SAI shutoff valve (vacuum or electric)

symptoms: Whirring noise on cold start (pump running)
No noise on cold start (pump not running)

fixSteps.title: Listen on cold start
fixSteps.instruction: From a fully cold start, listen near the SAI pump for ~60 seconds of whirring. No sound = pump or relay; constant sound = stuck-on relay.

fixSteps.title: Bench-test the pump
fixSteps.instruction: Apply battery voltage directly to the pump motor. Healthy pumps spin smoothly with strong airflow. Replace if seized, noisy, or weak.

fixSteps.title: Inspect check valves and shutoff valve
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the combi-valve assembly and check for carbon caking. Clean or replace, ensuring the diaphragm seals when no vacuum is applied.

fixSteps.title: Verify SAI relay and PCM driver
fixSteps.instruction: With a scan tool, command the SAI pump on. Verify 12V at the pump connector. If no command voltage, test the relay and PCM output.

faq.q: Will my car fail emissions?
faq.a: Yes — SAI is part of the OBD-II readiness monitors and the MIL must be off to pass.

faq.q: Is it safe to disable SAI?
faq.a: Disabling SAI is illegal in most jurisdictions and will not clear the readiness monitor. Repair the system instead.

fullDescription: Bank 1 sensor 1 cat temp signal stuck high. The secondary air injection system pumps fresh air into the exhaust during cold start to help the catalytic converter light off. Carbon build-up in the check valves and corrosion in the pump are the most common root causes — particularly in cold-climate vehicles.
safetyImpact: Vehicle remains drivable. Long-term, an SAI fault prevents catalyst warm-up and increases cold-start emissions.

causes.cause: Failed SAI pump (water ingress / brush wear)
Failed SAI shutoff valve (vacuum or electric)

symptoms: Whirring noise on cold start (pump running)
No noise on cold start (pump not running)

fixSteps.title: Listen on cold start
fixSteps.instruction: From a fully cold start, listen near the SAI pump for ~60 seconds of whirring. No sound = pump or relay; constant sound = stuck-on relay.

fixSteps.title: Bench-test the pump
fixSteps.instruction: Apply battery voltage directly to the pump motor. Healthy pumps spin smoothly with strong airflow. Replace if seized, noisy, or weak.

fixSteps.title: Inspect check valves and shutoff valve
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the combi-valve assembly and check for carbon caking. Clean or replace, ensuring the diaphragm seals when no vacuum is applied.

fixSteps.title: Verify SAI relay and PCM driver
fixSteps.instruction: With a scan tool, command the SAI pump on. Verify 12V at the pump connector. If no command voltage, test the relay and PCM output.

faq.q: Will my car fail emissions?
faq.a: Yes — SAI is part of the OBD-II readiness monitors and the MIL must be off to pass.

faq.q: Is it safe to disable SAI?
faq.a: Disabling SAI is illegal in most jurisdictions and will not clear the readiness monitor. Repair the system instead.
